transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, thank you very much, Jim, for this opportunity.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to thank Governor Romney and the University of Denver for your hospitality.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There are a lot of points I want to make tonight, but the most important one is that 20 years ago I became the luckiest man on Earth because Michelle Obama agreed to marry me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so I just want to wish, Sweetie, you happy anniversary and let you know that a year from now we will not be celebrating it in front of 40 million people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, four years ago we went through the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Millions of jobs were lost, the auto industry was on the brink of collapse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The financial system had frozen up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And because of the resilience and the determination of the American people, we’ve begun to fight our way back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Over the last 30 months, we’ve seen 5 million jobs in the private sector created.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The auto industry has come roaring back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And housing has begun to rise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But we all know that we’ve still got a lot of work to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so the question here tonight is not where we’ve been, but where we’re going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney has a perspective that says if we cut taxes, skewed towards the wealthy, and roll back regulations, that we’ll be better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve got a different view.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think we’ve got to invest in education and training.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s important for us to develop new sources of energy here in America, that we change our tax code to make sure that we’re helping small businesses and companies that are investing here in the United States, that we take some of the money that we’re saving as we wind down two wars to rebuild America and that we reduce our deficit in a balanced way that allows us to make these critical investments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, it ultimately is going to be up to the voters — to you — which path we should take.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Are we going to double on top-down economic policies that helped to get us into this mess or do we embrace a new economic patriotism that says America does best when the middle class does best?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’m looking forward to having that debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s an honor to be here with you, and I appreciate the chance to be with the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m pleased to be at the University of Denver, appreciate their welcome, and also the Presidential Commission on these debates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And congratulations to you, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, on your anniversary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m sure this was the most romantic place you could imagine, here — here with me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So I… Congratulations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is obviously a very tender topic.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve had the occasion over the last couple of years of meeting people across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was in Dayton, Ohio, and a woman grabbed my arm and she said, “I’ve been out of work since May.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Can you help me?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” Ann yesterday was at a rally in Denver and a woman came up to her with a baby in her arms and said, “Ann, my husband has had four jobs in three years, part-time jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He’s lost his most recent job and we’ve now just lost our home.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Can you help us?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” And the answer is, yes, we can help, but it’s going to take a different path.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Not the one we’ve been on, not the one the president describes as a top-down, cut taxes for the rich.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s not what I’m going to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My plan has five basic parts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One, get us energy independent, North American energy independent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That creates about 4 million jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, open up more trade, particularly in Latin America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Crack down on China, if and when they cheat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number three, make sure our people have the skills they need to succeed and the best schools in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re far away from that now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number four, get to us a balanced budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number five, champion small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s small business that creates the jobs in America, and over the last four years, small business people have decided that America may not be the place to open a new business because new business startups are down to a 30-year low.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’m concerned that the path that we’re on has just been unsuccessful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president has a view very similar to the view he had when he ran four years, that a bigger government, spending more, taxing more, regulating more — if you will, trickle-down government — would work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s not the right answer for America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll restore the vitality that gets America working again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, let me talk specifically about what I think we need to do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First, we’ve got to improve our education system and we’ve made enormous progress drawing on ideas both from Democrats and Republicans that are already starting to show gains in some of the toughest to deal with schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got a program called Race to the Top that has prompted reforms in 46 states around the country, raising standards, improving how we train teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So now I want to hire another 100,000 new math and science teachers, and create 2 million more slots in our community colleges so that people can get trained for the jobs that are out there right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I want to make sure that we keep tuition low for our young people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to our tax code, Governor Romney and I both agree that our corporate tax rate is too high, so I want to lower it, particularly for manufacturing, taking it down to 25 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I also want to close those loopholes that are giving incentives for companies that are shipping jobs overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I want to provide tax breaks for companies that are investing here in the United States.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: On energy, Governor Romney and I, we both agree that we’ve got to boost American energy production, and oil and natural gas production are higher than they’ve been in years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I also believe that we’ve got to look at the energy sources of the future, like wind and solar and biofuels, and make those investments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So all of this is possible.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, in order for us to do it, we do have to close our deficit, and one of the things I’m sure we’ll be discussing tonight is, how do we deal with our tax code?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And how do we make sure that we are reducing spending in a responsible way, but also, how do we have enough revenue to make those investments?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is where there’s a difference, because Governor Romney’s central economic plan calls for a $5 trillion tax cut — on top of the extension of the Bush tax cuts — that’s another trillion dollars — and $2 trillion in additional military spending that the military hasn’t asked for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s $8 trillion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: How we pay for that, reduce the deficit, and make the investments that we need to make, without dumping those costs onto middle-class Americans, I think is one of the central questions of this campaign.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, sure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d like to clear up the record and go through it piece by piece.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I don’t have a $5 trillion tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have a tax cut of a scale that you’re talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My view is that we ought to provide tax relief to people in the middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I’m not going to reduce the share of taxes paid by high-income people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: High-income people are doing just fine in this economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’ll do fine whether you’re president or I am.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The people who are having the hard time right now are middle- income Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Under the president’s policies, middle-income Americans have been buried.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re just being crushed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Middle- income Americans have seen their income come down by $4,300.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is a — this is a tax in and of itself.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll call it the economy tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s been crushing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: At the same time, gasoline prices have doubled under the president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Electric rates are up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Food prices are up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Health care costs have gone up by $2,500 a family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Middle-income families are being crushed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so the question is how to get them going again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve described it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s energy and trade, the right kind of training programs, balancing our budget and helping small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Those are the — the cornerstones of my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the president mentioned a couple of other ideas I’ll just note.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First, education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I agree: Education is key, particularly the future of our economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But our training programs right now, we’ve got 47 of them, housed in the federal government, reporting to eight different agencies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Overhead is overwhelming.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got to get those dollars back to the states and go to the workers so they can create their own pathways to get in the training they need for jobs that will really help them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The second area, taxation, we agree, we ought to bring the tax rates down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I do, both for corporations and for individuals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But in order for us not to lose revenue, have the government run out of money, I also lower deductions and credits and exemptions, so that we keep taking in the same money when you also account for growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The third area, energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Energy is critical, and the president pointed out correctly that production of oil and gas in the U.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: is up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But not due to his policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In spite of his policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, all of the increase in natural gas and oil has happened on private land, not on government land.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: On government land, your administration has cut the number of permits and licenses in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If I’m president, I’ll double them, and also get the — the oil from offshore and Alaska.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I’ll bring that pipeline in from Canada.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And, by the way, I like coal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to make sure we can continue to burn clean coal.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: People in the coal industry feel like it’s getting crushed by your policies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to get America and North America energy independent so we can create those jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And finally, with regards to that tax cut, look, I’m not looking to cut massive taxes and to reduce the — the revenues going to the government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My — my number-one principal is, there will be no tax cut that adds to the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to underline that: no tax cut that adds to the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I do want to reduce the burden being paid by middle-income Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I — and to do that, that also means I cannot reduce the burden paid by high-income Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So any — any language to the contrary is simply not accurate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: LEHRER: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I think — let’s talk about taxes, because I think it’s instructive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, four years ago, when I stood on this stage, I said that I would cut taxes for middle-class families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s exactly what I did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We cut taxes for middle-class families by about $3,600.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason is, because I believe that we do best when the middle class is doing well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And by giving them those tax cuts, they had a little more money in their pocket, and so maybe they can buy a new car.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They are certainly in a better position to weather the extraordinary recession that we went through.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They can buy a computer for their kid who’s going off to college, which means they’re spending more money, businesses have more customers, businesses make more profits, and then hire more workers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney’s proposal that he has been promoting for 18 months calls for a $5 trillion tax cut, on top of $2 trillion of additional spending for our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And he is saying that he is going to pay for it by closing loopholes and deductions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The problem is that he’s been asked over 100 times how you would close those deductions and loopholes, and he hasn’t been able to identify them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I’m going to make an important point here, Jim.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When you add up all the loopholes and deductions that upper-income individuals can — are currently taking advantage of, you take those all away, you don’t come close to paying for $5 trillion in tax cuts and $2 trillion in additional military spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why independent studies looking at this said the only way to meet Governor Romney’s pledge of not reducing the deficit or — or — or not adding to the deficit is by burdening middle-class families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The average middle-class family with children would pay about $2,000 more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, that’s not my analysis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the analysis of economists who have looked at this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And — and that kind of top — top-down economics, where folks at the top are doing well, so the average person making $3 million is getting a $250,000 tax break, while middle-class families are burdened further, that’s not what I believe is a recipe for economic growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, but — but virtually — virtually everything he just said about my tax plan is inaccurate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So if the tax plan he described were a tax plan I was asked to support, I’d say absolutely not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m not looking for a $5 trillion tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What I’ve said is I won’t put in place a tax cut that adds to the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s part one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So there’s no economist that can say Mitt Romney’s tax plan adds $5 trillion if I say I will not add to the deficit with my tax plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, I will not reduce the share paid by high-income individuals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know that you and your running mate keep saying that and I know it’s a popular thing to say with a lot of people, but it’s just not the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, I’ve got five boys.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m used to people saying something that’s not always true, but just keep on repeating it and ultimately hoping I’ll believe it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But that — that is not the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: All right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will not reduce the taxes paid by high-income Americans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And number three, I will not under any circumstances raise taxes on middle-income families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will lower taxes on middle-income families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, you cite a study.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There are six other studies that looked at the study you describe and say it’s completely wrong.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I saw a study that came out today that said you’re going to raise taxes by $3,000 to $4,000 on middle-income families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There are all these studies out there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But let’s get at the bottom line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That is, I want to bring down rates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to bring the rates down, at the same time lower deductions and exemptions and credits and so forth, so we keep getting the revenue we need.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And you’d think, well, then why lower the rates?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the reason is because small business pays that individual rate; 54 percent of America’s workers work in businesses that are taxed not at the corporate tax rate, but at the individual tax rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And if we lower that rate, they will be able to hire more people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: For me, this is about jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is about getting jobs for the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, for 18 months he’s been running on this tax plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And now, five weeks before the election, he’s saying that his big, bold idea is, “Never mind.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” And the fact is that if you are lowering the rates the way you described, Governor, then it is not possible to come up with enough deductions and loopholes that only affect high-income individuals to avoid either raising the deficit or burdening the middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s — it’s math.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s arithmetic.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney and I do share a deep interest in encouraging small-business growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So at the same time that my tax plan has already lowered taxes for 98 percent of families, I also lowered taxes for small businesses 18 times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And what I want to do is continue the tax rates — the tax cuts that we put into place for small businesses and families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I have said that for incomes over $250,000 a year, that we should go back to the rates that we had when Bill Clinton was president, when we created 23 million new jobs, went from deficit to surplus, and created a whole lot of millionaires to boot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason this is important is because by doing that, we cannot only reduce the deficit, we cannot only encourage job growth through small businesses, but we’re also able to make the investments that are necessary in education or in energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we do have a difference, though, when it comes to definitions of small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Under — under my plan, 97 percent of small businesses would not see their income taxes go up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney says, well, those top 3 percent, they’re the job creators, they’d be burdened.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But under Governor Romney’s definition, there are a whole bunch of millionaires and billionaires who are small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Donald Trump is a small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, I know Donald Trump doesn’t like to think of himself as small anything, but — but that’s how you define small businesses if you’re getting business income.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that kind of approach, I believe, will not grow our economy, because the only way to pay for it without either burdening the middle class or blowing up our deficit is to make drastic cuts in things like education, making sure that we are continuing to invest in basic science and research, all the things that are helping America grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I think that would be a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Jim, let me just come back on that — on that point, which is these…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … the small businesses we’re talking about…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s fun, isn’t it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You bet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, President, you’re — Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, you’re absolutely right, which is that, with regards to 97 percent of the businesses are not — not taxed at the 35 percent tax rate, they’re taxed at a lower rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But those businesses that are in the last 3 percent of businesses happen to employ half — half of all the people who work in small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Those are the businesses that employ one-quarter of all the workers in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And your plan is to take their tax rate from 35 percent to 40 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, and — and I’ve talked to a guy who has a very small business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He’s in the electronics business in — in St.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Louis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He has four employees.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said he and his son calculated how much they pay in taxes, federal income tax, federal payroll tax, state income tax, state sales tax, state property tax, gasoline tax.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It added up to well over 50 percent of what they earned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And your plan is to take the tax rate on successful small businesses from 35 percent to 40 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The National Federation of Independent Businesses has said that will cost 700,000 jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to cost jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My priority is jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so what I do is I bring down the tax rates, lower deductions and exemptions, the same idea behind Bowles-Simpson, by the way, get the rates down, lower deductions and exemptions, to create more jobs, because there’s nothing better for getting us to a balanced budget than having more people working, earning more money, paying more taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s by far the most effective and efficient way to get this budget balanced.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Jim, I — you may want to move onto another topic, but I — I would just say this to the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If you believe that we can cut taxes by $5 trillion and add $2 trillion in additional spending that the military is not asking for, $7 trillion — just to give you a sense, over 10 years, that’s more than our entire defense budget — and you think that by closing loopholes and deductions for the well-to-do, somehow you will not end up picking up the tab, then Governor Romney’s plan may work for you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I think math, common sense, and our history shows us that’s not a recipe for job growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, we’ve tried this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve tried both approaches.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The approach that Governor Romney’s talking about is the same sales pitch that was made in 2001 and 2003, and we ended up with the slowest job growth in 50 years, we ended up moving from surplus to deficits, and it all culminated in the worst financial crisis since the Great Depression.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Bill Clinton tried the approach that I’m talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We created 23 million new jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We went from deficit to surplus.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And businesses did very well.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So, in some ways, we’ve got some data on which approach is more likely to create jobs and opportunity for Americans and I believe that the economy works best when middle-class families are getting tax breaks so that they’ve got some money in their pockets, and those of us who have done extraordinarily well because of this magnificent country that we live in, that we can afford to do a little bit more to make sure we’re not blowing up the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Jim, the president began this segment, so I think I get the last word.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: All right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, but he gets the first word of that segment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I get the last word I hope.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me just make this comment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think first of all, let me — let me repeat — let me repeat what I said.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m not in favor of a $5 trillion tax cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s not my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My plan is not to put in place any tax cut that will add to the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s point one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So you may keep referring to it as a $5 trillion tax cut, but that’s not my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, let’s look at history.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My plan is not like anything that’s been tried before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My plan is to bring down rates, but also bring down deductions and exemptions and credits at the same time so the revenue stays in, but that we bring down rates to get more people working.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My priority is putting people back to work in America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re suffering in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And we talk about evidence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look at the evidence of the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s absolutely extraordinary.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve got 23 million people out of work or stopped looking for work in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s just — it’s — we’ve got — when the president took office, 32 million people on food stamps; 47 million on food stamps today; economic growth this year slower than last year, and last year slower than the year before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Going forward with the status quo is not going to cut it for the American people who are struggling today.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m glad you raised that, and it’s a — it’s a critical issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s not just an economic issue, I think it’s a moral issue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think it’s, frankly, not moral for my generation to keep spending massively more than we take in, knowing those burdens are going to be passed on to the next generation and they’re going to be paying the interest and the principal all their lives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the amount of debt we’re adding, at a trillion a year, is simply not moral.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So how do we deal with it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, mathematically, there are three ways that you can cut a deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One, of course, is to raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two is to cut spending.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And number is to grow the economy, because if more people work in a growing economy, they’re paying taxes, and you can get the job done that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The presidents would — president would prefer raising taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The problem with raising taxes is that it slows down the rate of growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And you could never quite get the job done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to lower spending and encourage economic growth at the same time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What things would I cut from spending?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I will eliminate all programs by this test, if they don’t pass it: Is the program so critical it’s worth borrowing money from China to pay for it?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And if not, I’ll get rid of it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Obamacare’s on my list.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I apologize, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I use that term with all respect, by the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I like it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: OK, good.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So I’ll get rid of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry, Jim, I’m going to stop the subsidy to PBS.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m going to stop other things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I like PBS, I love Big Bird.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Actually like you, too.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I’m not going to — I’m not going to keep on spending money on things to borrow money from China to pay for.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, I’ll take programs that are currently good programs but I think could be run more efficiently at the state level and send them to the state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number three, I’ll make government more efficient and to cut back the number of employees, combine some agencies and departments.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My cutbacks will be done through attrition, by the way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is the approach we have to take to get America to a balanced budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president said he’d cut the deficit in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Unfortunately, he doubled it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Trillion-dollar deficits for the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s put it in place as much public debt — almost as much debt held by the public as al prior presidents combined.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When I walked into the Oval Office, I had more than a trillion-dollar deficit greeting me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we know where it came from: two wars that were paid for on a credit card; two tax cuts that were not paid for; and a whole bunch of programs that were not paid for; and then a massive economic crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And despite that, what we’ve said is, yes, we had to take some initial emergency measures to make sure we didn’t slip into a Great Depression, but what we’ve also said is, let’s make sure that we are cutting out those things that are not helping us grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So 77 government programs, everything from aircrafts that the Air Force had ordered but weren’t working very well, 18 government — 18 government programs for education that were well-intentioned, not weren’t helping kids learn, we went after medical fraud in Medicare and Medicaid very aggressively, more aggressively than ever before, and have saved tens of billions of dollars, $50 billion of waste taken out of the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I worked with Democrats and Republicans to cut a trillion dollars out of our discretionary domestic budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s the largest cut in the discretionary domestic budget since Dwight Eisenhower.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, we all know that we’ve got to do more.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so I’ve put forward a specific $4 trillion deficit reduction plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s on a website.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You can look at all the numbers, what cuts we make and what revenue we raise.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the way we do it is $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: 50 for every cut, we ask for $1 of additional revenue, paid for, as I indicated earlier, by asking those of us who have done very well in this country to contribute a little bit more to reduce the deficit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney earlier mentioned the Bowles-Simpson commission.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, that’s how the commission — bipartisan commission that talked about how we should move forward suggested we have to do it, in a balanced way with some revenue and some spending cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is a major difference that Governor Romney and I have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let — let me just finish their point, because you’re looking for contrast.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, when Governor Romney stood on a stage with other Republican candidates for the nomination and he was asked, would you take $10 of spending cuts for just $1 of revenue?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And he said no.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, if you take such an unbalanced approach, then that means you are going to be gutting our investments in schools and education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It means that Governor Romney…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … talked about Medicaid and how we could send it back to the states, but effectively this means a 30 percent cut in the primary program we help for seniors who are in nursing homes, for kids who are with disabilities.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And — and that is not a right strategy for us to move forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Simpson-Bowles, the president should have grabbed that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I have my own plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s not the same as Simpson- Bowles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But in my view, the president should have grabbed it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If you wanted to make some adjustments to it, take it, go to Congress, fight for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what we’ve done, made some adjustments to it, and we’re putting it forward before Congress right now, a $4 trillion plan…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But you’ve been — but you’ve been president four years…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ve been president four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You said you’d cut the deficit in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s now four years later.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We still have trillion-dollar deficits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The CBO says we’ll have a trillion-dollar deficit each of the next four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If you’re re-elected, we’ll get to a trillion-dollar debt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I mean, you have said before you’d cut the deficit in half.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And this — I love this idea of $4 trillion in cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You found $4 trillion of ways to reduce or to get closer to a balanced budget, except we still show trillion-dollar deficits every year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That doesn’t get the job done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me come back and say, why is it that I don’t want to raise taxes?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Why don’t I want to raise taxes on people?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And actually, you said it back in 2010.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You said, “Look, I’m going to extend the tax policies that we have now; I’m not going to raise taxes on anyone, because when the economy is growing slow like this, when we’re in recession, you shouldn’t raise taxes on anyone.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” Well, the economy is still growing slow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, it’s growing much more slowly now than when you made that statement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so if you believe the same thing, you just don’t want to raise taxes on people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the reality is it’s not just wealthy people — you mentioned Donald Trump.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s not just Donald Trump you’re taxing.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s all those businesses that employ one-quarter of the workers in America; these small businesses that are taxed as individuals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You raise taxes and you kill jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s why the National Federation of Independent Businesses said your plan will kill 700,000 jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to kill jobs in this environment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll make one more point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, we’ve had this discussion before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There has to be revenue in addition to cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney has ruled out revenue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He’s ruled out revenue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, the revenue I get is by more people working, getting higher pay, paying more taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s how we get growth and how we balance the budget.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the idea of taxing people more, putting more people out of work, you’ll never get there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ll never balance the budget by raising taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Spain — Spain spends 42 percent of their total economy on government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re now spending 42 percent of our economy on government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to go down the path to Spain.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to go down the path of growth that puts Americans to work with more money coming in because they’re working.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: If — if we’re serious, we’ve got to take a balanced, responsible approach.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, this is not just when it comes to individual taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk about corporate taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, I’ve identified areas where we can, right away, make a change that I believe would actually help the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The oil industry gets $4 billion a year in corporate welfare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Basically, they get deductions that those small businesses that Governor Romney refers to, they don’t get.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, does anybody think that ExxonMobil needs some extra money, when they’re making money every time you go to the pump?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Why wouldn’t we want to eliminate that?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Why wouldn’t we eliminate tax breaks for corporate jets?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: My attitude is, if you got a corporate jet, you can probably afford to pay full freight, not get a special break for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to corporate taxes, Governor Romney has said he wants to, in a revenue neutral way, close loopholes, deductions — he hasn’t identified which ones they are — but that thereby bring down the corporate rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I want to do the same thing, but I’ve actually identified how we can do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And part of the way to do it is to not give tax breaks to companies that are shipping jobs overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Right now, you can actually take a deduction for moving a plant overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think most Americans would say that doesn’t make sense.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And all that raises revenue.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so if we take a balanced approach, what that then allows us to do is also to help young people, the way we already have during my administration, make sure that they can afford to go to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It means that the teacher that I met in Las Vegas, a wonderful young lady, who describes to me — she’s got 42 kids in her class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The first two weeks she’s got them, some of them sitting on the floor until finally they get reassigned.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’re using text books that are 10 years old.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That is not a recipe for growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s not how America was built.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so budgets reflect choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Ultimately, we’re going to have to make some decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if we’re asking for no revenue, then that means that we’ve got to get rid of a whole bunch of stuff.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the magnitude of the tax cuts that you’re talking about, Governor, would end up resulting in severe hardship for people, but more importantly, would not help us grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: As I indicated before, when you talk about shifting Medicaid to states, we’re talking about potentially a 30 — a 30 percent cut in Medicaid over time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, you know, that may not seem like a big deal when it just is, you know, numbers on a sheet of paper, but if we’re talking about a family who’s got an autistic kid and is depending on that Medicaid, that’s a big problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And governors are creative.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There’s no doubt about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But they’re not creative enough to make up for 30 percent of revenue on something like Medicaid.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What ends up happening is some people end up not getting help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Jim, let’s — we’ve gone on a lot of topics there, and so it’s going to take a minute to go from Medicaid to schools…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … to oil, to tax breaks, then companies going overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So let’s go through them one by one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First of all, the Department of Energy has said the tax break for oil companies is $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 8 billion a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And it’s actually an accounting treatment, as you know, that’s been in place for a hundred years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s time to end it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And in one year, you provided $90 billion in breaks to the green energy world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, I like green energy as well, but that’s about 50 years’ worth of what oil and gas receives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And you say Exxon and Mobil.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Actually, this $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 8 billion goes largely to small companies, to drilling operators and so forth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But, you know, if we get that tax rate from 35 percent down to 25 percent, why that $2.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: 8 billion is on the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Of course it’s on the table.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s probably not going to survive you get that rate down to 25 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But don’t forget, you put $90 billion, like 50 years’ worth of breaks, into — into solar and wind, to Solyndra and Fisker and Tester and Ener1.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I mean, I had a friend who said you don’t just pick the winners and losers, you pick the losers, all right?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So this — this is not — this is not the kind of policy you want to have if you want to get America energy secure.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The second topic, which is you said you get a deduction for taking a plant overseas.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, I’ve been in business for 25 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I have no idea what you’re talking about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I maybe need to get a new accountant.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But — but the idea that you get a break for shipping jobs overseas is simply not the case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What we do have right now is a setting where I’d like to bring money from overseas back to this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And, finally, Medicaid to states?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m not quite sure where that came in, except this, which is, I would like to take the Medicaid dollars that go to states and say to a state, you’re going to get what you got last year, plus inflation, plus 1 percent, and then you’re going to manage your care for your poor in the way you think best.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I remember, as a governor, when this idea was floated by Tommy Thompson, the governors — Republican and Democrats — said, please let us do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We can care for our own poor in so much better and more effective a way than having the federal government tell us how to care for our poor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So — so let’s state — one of the magnificent things about this country is the whole idea that states are the laboratories of democracy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Don’t have the federal government tell everybody what kind of training programs they have to have and what kind of Medicaid they have to have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let states do this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And, by the way, if a state gets in trouble, well, we can step in and see if we can find a way to help them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But — but the right — the right approach is one which relies on the brilliance of our people and states, not the federal government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: OK.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, I suspect that, on Social Security, we’ve got a somewhat similar position.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Social Security is structurally sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s going to have to be tweaked the way it was by Ronald Reagan and Speaker — Democratic Speaker Tip O’Neill.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But it is — the basic structure is sound.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But — but I want to talk about the values behind Social Security and Medicare, and then talk about Medicare, because that’s the big driver of our deficits right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, my grandmother — some of you know — helped to raise me.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: My grandparents did.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: My grandfather died a while back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: My grandmother died three days before I was elected president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And she was fiercely independent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: She worked her way up, only had a high school education, started as a secretary, ended up being the vice president of a local bank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And she ended up living alone by choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason she could be independent was because of Social Security and Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: She had worked all her life, put in this money, and understood that there was a basic guarantee, a floor under which she could not go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s the perspective I bring when I think about what’s called entitlements.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, the name itself implies some sense of dependency on the part of these folks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: These are folks who’ve worked hard, like my grandmother, and there are millions of people out there who are counting on this.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So my approach is to say, how do we strengthen the system over the long term?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And in Medicare, what we did was we said, we are going to have to bring down the costs if we’re going to deal with our long-term deficits, but to do that, let’s look where some of the money’s going.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: $716 billion we were able to save from the Medicare program by no longer overpaying insurance companies by making sure that we weren’t overpaying providers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And using that money, we were actually able to lower prescription drug costs for seniors by an average of $600, and we were also able to make a — make a significant dent in providing them the kind of preventive care that will ultimately save money through the — throughout the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So the way for us to deal with Medicare in particular is to lower health care costs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to Social Security, as I said, you don’t need a major structural change in order to make sure that Social Security is there for the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, Jim, our seniors depend on these programs, and I know anytime we talk about entitlements, people become concerned that something’s going to happen that’s going to change their life for the worse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the answer is neither the president nor I are proposing any changes for any current retirees or near retirees, either to Social Security or Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So if you’re 60 or around 60 or older, you don’t need to listen any further.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But for younger people, we need to talk about what changes are going to be occurring.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Oh, I just thought about one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that is, in fact, I was wrong when I said the president isn’t proposing any changes for current retirees.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In fact he is on Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: On Social Security he’s not.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But on Medicare, for current retirees, he’s cutting $716 billion from the program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, he says by not overpaying hospitals and providers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Actually just going to them and saying, “We’re going to reduce the rates you get paid across the board, everybody’s going to get a lower rate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: ” That’s not just going after places where there’s abuse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s saying we’re cutting the rates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Some 15 percent of hospitals and nursing homes say they won’t take anymore Medicare patients under that scenario.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We also have 50 percent of doctors who say they won’t take more Medicare patients.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This — we have 4 million people on Medicare Advantage that will lose Medicare Advantage because of those $716 billion in cuts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I can’t understand how you can cut Medicare $716 billion for current recipients of Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Now, you point out, well, we’re putting some back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re going to give a better prescription program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s $1 — that’s $1 for every $15 you’ve cut.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re smart enough to know that’s not a good trade.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to take that $716 billion you’ve cut and put it back into Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: By the way, we can include a prescription program if we need to improve it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the idea of cutting $716 billion from Medicare to be able to balance the additional cost of Obamacare is, in my opinion, a mistake.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And with regards to young people coming along, I’ve got proposals to make sure Medicare and Social Security are there for them without any question.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I think it’s important for Governor Romney to present this plan that he says will only affect folks in the future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the essence of the plan is that you would turn Medicare into a voucher program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s called premium support, but it’s understood to be a voucher program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: His running mate…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I don’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And let me explain why.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Again, that’s for future…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I understand.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: … people, right, not for current retirees.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: For — so if you’re — if you’re 54 or 55, you might want to listen ’cause this — this will affect you.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The idea, which was originally presented by Congressman Ryan, your running mate, is that we would give a voucher to seniors and they could go out in the private marketplace and buy their own health insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The problem is that because the voucher wouldn’t necessarily keep up with health care inflation, it was estimated that this would cost the average senior about $6,000 a year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, in fairness, what Governor Romney has now said is he’ll maintain traditional Medicare alongside it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But there’s still a problem, because what happens is, those insurance companies are pretty clever at figuring out who are the younger and healthier seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They recruit them, leaving the older, sicker seniors in Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And every health care economist that looks at it says, over time, what’ll happen is the traditional Medicare system will collapse.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And then what you’ve got is folks like my grandmother at the mercy of the private insurance system precisely at the time when they are most in need of decent health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So, I don’t think vouchers are the right way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is not my own — only my opinion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: AARP thinks that the — the savings that we obtained from Medicare bolster the system, lengthen the Medicare trust fund by eight years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Benefits were not affected at all.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And ironically, if you repeal Obamacare, and I have become fond of this term, “Obamacare,” if you repeal it, what happens is those seniors right away are going to be paying $600 more in prescription care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They’re now going to have to be paying copays for basic checkups that can keep them healthier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the primary beneficiary of that repeal are insurance companies that are estimated to gain billions of dollars back when they aren’t making seniors any healthier.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I don’t think that’s the right approach when it comes to making sure that Medicare is stronger over the long term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What I support is no change for current retirees and near-retirees to Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the president supports taking $716 billion out of that program.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So that’s — that’s number one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two is for people coming along that are young, what I do to make sure that we can keep Medicare in place for them is to allow them either to choose the current Medicare program or a private plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Their choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They get to choose — and they’ll have at least two plans that will be entirely at no cost to them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So they don’t have to pay additional money, no additional $6,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s not going to happen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’ll have at least two plans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, if the government can be as efficient as the private sector and offer premiums that are as low as the private sector, people will be happy to get traditional Medicare or they’ll be able to get a private plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I know my own view is I’d rather have a private plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d just assume not have the government telling me what kind of health care I get.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’d rather be able to have an insurance company.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If I don’t like them, I can get rid of them and find a different insurance company.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But people make their own choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The other thing we have to do to save Medicare?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to have the benefits high for those that are low income, but for higher income people, we’re going to have to lower some of the benefits.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to make sure this program is there for the long term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s the plan that I’ve put forward.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And, by the way the idea came not even from Paul Ryan or — or Senator Wyden, who’s the co-author of the bill with — with Paul Ryan in the Senate, but also it came from Bill — Bill Clinton’s chief of staff.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is an idea that’s been around a long time, which is saying, hey, let’s see if we can’t get competition into the Medicare world so that people can get the choice of different plans at lower cost, better quality.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I believe in competition.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Jim, if I — if I can just respond very quickly, first of all, every study has shown that Medicare has lower administrative costs than private insurance does, which is why seniors are generally pretty happy with it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And private insurers have to make a profit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Nothing wrong with that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s what they do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so you’ve got higher administrative costs, plus profit on top of that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And if you are going to save any money through what Governor Romney’s proposing, what has to happen is, is that the money has to come from somewhere.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when you move to a voucher system, you are putting seniors at the mercy of those insurance companies.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And over time, if traditional Medicare has decayed or fallen apart, then they’re stuck.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is the reason why AARP has said that your plan would weaken Medicare substantially.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s why they were supportive of the approach that we took.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: One last point I want to make.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We do have to lower the cost of health care, not just in Medicare and Medicaid… LEHRER: Talk about that in a minute.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … but — but — but overall.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s — that’s a big topic.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Can we — can we stay on Medicare?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Is that a — is that a separate topic?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’m sorry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s get back to Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s get back to Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president said that the government can provide the service at lower cost and without a profit.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If that’s the case, then it will always be the best product that people can purchase.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But my experience — my experience the private sector typically is able to provide a better product at a lower cost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Regulation is essential.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You can’t have a free market work if you don’t have regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As a businessperson, I had to have — I need to know the regulations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I needed them there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You couldn’t have people opening up banks in their — in their garage and making loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I mean, you have to have regulations so that you can have an economy work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Every free economy has good regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: At the same time, regulation can become excessive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In some places, yes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Other places, no.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No, it can become out of date.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And what’s happened with some of the legislation that’s been passed during the president’s term, you’ve seen regulation become excessive, and it’s hurt — it’s hurt the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me give you an example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Dodd-Frank was passed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
