transcript_turns.text: And it includes within it a number of provisions that I think has some unintended consequences that are harmful to the economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One is it designates a number of banks as too big to fail, and they’re effectively guaranteed by the federal government.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is the biggest kiss that’s been given to — to New York banks I’ve ever seen.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is an enormous boon for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There’ve been 122 community and small banks have closed since Dodd- Frank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So there’s one example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Here’s another.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In Dodd-Frank…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, I would repeal and replace it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re not going to get rid of all regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You have to have regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And there are some parts of Dodd-Frank that make all the sense in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You need transparency, you need to have leverage limits for…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But let’s — let’s mention — let me mention the other one.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s talk…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I think this is a great example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The reason we have been in such a enormous economic crisis was prompted by reckless behavior across the board.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, it wasn’t just on Wall Street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You had loan officers were — that were giving loans and mortgages that really shouldn’t have been given, because the folks didn’t qualify.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You had people who were borrowing money to buy a house that they couldn’t afford.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You had credit agencies that were stamping these as A1 great investments when they weren’t.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But you also had banks making money hand over fist, churning out products that the bankers themselves didn’t even understand, in order to make big profits, but knowing that it made the entire system vulnerable.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So what did we do?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We stepped in and had the toughest reforms on Wall Street since the 1930s.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We said you’ve got — banks, you’ve got to raise your capital requirements.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You can’t engage in some of this risky behavior that is putting Main Street at risk.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We’ve going to make sure that you’ve got to have a living will so — so we can know how you’re going to wind things down if you make a bad bet so we don’t have other taxpayer bailouts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the meantime, by the way, we also made sure that all the help that we provided those banks was paid back every single dime, with interest.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, Governor Romney has said he wants to repeal Dodd-Frank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, I appreciate and it appears we’ve got some agreement that a marketplace to work has to have some regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But in the past, Governor Romney has said he just want to repeal Dodd- Frank, roll it back.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so the question is: Does anybody out there think that the big problem we had is that there was too much oversight and regulation of Wall Street?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because if you do, then Governor Romney is your candidate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But that’s not what I believe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Sorry, but that’s just not — that’s just not the facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, we have to have regulation on Wall Street.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s why I’d have regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But I wouldn’t designate five banks as too big to fail and give them a blank check.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s one of the unintended consequences of Dodd-Frank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It wasn’t thought through properly.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We need to get rid of that provision because it’s killing regional and small banks.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They’re getting hurt.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let me mention another regulation in Dodd-Frank.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You say we were giving mortgages to people who weren’t qualified.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s exactly right.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s one of the reasons for the great financial calamity we had.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And so Dodd-Frank correctly says we need to have qualified mortgages, and if you give a mortgage that’s not qualified, there are big penalties, except they didn’t ever go on and define what a qualified mortgage was.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s been two years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We don’t know what a qualified mortgage is yet.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So banks are reluctant to make loans, mortgages.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Try and get a mortgage these days.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s hurt the housing market because Dodd-Frank didn’t anticipate putting in place the kinds of regulations you have to have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s not that Dodd-Frank always was wrong with too much regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Sometimes they didn’t come out with a clear regulation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will make sure we don’t hurt the functioning of our — of our marketplace and our business, because I want to bring back housing and get good jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I sure do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, in part, it comes, again, from my experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You know, I was in New Hampshire.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: A woman came to me and she said, look, I can’t afford insurance for myself or my son.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I met a couple in Appleton, Wisconsin, and they said, we’re thinking of dropping our insurance, we can’t afford it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the number of small businesses I’ve gone to that are saying they’re dropping insurance because they can’t afford it, the cost of health care is just prohibitive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And — and we’ve got to deal with cost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And, unfortunately, when — when — when you look at Obamacare, the Congressional Budget Office has said it will cost $2,500 a year more than traditional insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So it’s adding to cost.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And as a matter of fact, when the president ran for office, he said that, by this year, he would have brought down the cost of insurance for each family by $2,500 a family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Instead, it’s gone up by that amount.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So it’s expensive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Expensive things hurt families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So that’s one reason I don’t want it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Second reason, it cuts $716 billion from Medicare to pay for it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to put that money back in Medicare for our seniors.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number three, it puts in place an unelected board that’s going to tell people ultimately what kind of treatments they can have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t like that idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Fourth, there was a survey done of small businesses across the country, said, what’s been the effect of Obamacare on your hiring plans?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And three-quarters of them said it makes us less likely to hire people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I just don’t know how the president could have come into office, facing 23 million people out of work, rising unemployment, an economic crisis at the — at the kitchen table, and spend his energy and passion for two years fighting for Obamacare instead of fighting for jobs for the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It has killed jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the best course for health care is to do what we did in my state: craft a plan at the state level that fits the needs of the state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then let’s focus on getting the costs down for people, rather than raising it with the $2,500 additional premium.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No, I think — I had five seconds before you interrupted me, was … … the irony is that we’ve seen this model work really well in Massachusetts, because Governor Romney did a good thing, working with Democrats in the state to set up what is essentially the identical model and as a consequence people are covered there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It hasn’t destroyed jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as a consequence, we now have a system in which we have the opportunity to start bringing down costs, as opposed to just leaving millions of people out in the cold.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, I did with my first statement.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First of all, I like the way we did it in Massachusetts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I like the fact that in my state, we had Republicans and Democrats come together and work together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What you did instead was to push through a plan without a single Republican vote.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, when Massachusetts did something quite extraordinary — elected a Republican senator to stop Obamacare, you pushed it through anyway.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So entirely on a partisan basis, instead of bringing America together and having a discussion on this important topic, you pushed through something that you and Nancy Pelosi and Harry Reid thought was the best answer and drove it through.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What we did in a legislature 87 percent Democrat, we worked together; 200 legislators in my legislature, only two voted against the plan by the time we were finished.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What were some differences?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t raise taxes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ve raised them by $1 trillion under Obamacare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t cut Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Of course, we don’t have Medicare, but we didn’t cut Medicare by $716 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t put in place a board that can tell people ultimately what treatments they’re going to receive.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We didn’t also do something that I think a number of people across this country recognize, which is put — put people in a position where they’re going to lose the insurance they had and they wanted.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Right now, the CBO says up to 20 million people will lose their insurance as Obamacare goes into effect next year.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And likewise, a study by McKinsey and Company of American businesses said 30 percent of them are anticipating dropping people from coverage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So for those reasons, for the tax, for Medicare, for this board, and for people losing their insurance, this is why the American people don’t want Medicare — don’t want Obamacare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s why Republicans said, do not do this, and the Republicans had — had the plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They put a plan out.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: They put out a plan, a bipartisan plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It was swept aside.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I think something this big, this important has to be done on a bipartisan basis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And we have to have a president who can reach across the aisle and fashion important legislation with the input from both parties.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney said this has to be done on a bipartisan basis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This was a bipartisan idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, it was a Republican idea.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And Governor Romney at the beginning of this debate wrote and said what we did in Massachusetts could be a model for the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I agree that the Democratic legislators in Massachusetts might have given some advice to Republicans in Congress about how to cooperate, but the fact of the matter is, we used the same advisers, and they say it’s the same plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It — when Governor Romney talks about this board, for example, unelected board that we’ve created, what this is, is a group of health care experts, doctors, et cetera, to figure out, how can we reduce the cost of care in the system overall?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Because there — there are two ways of dealing with our health care crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: One is to simply leave a whole bunch of people uninsured and let them fend for themselves, to let businesses figure out how long they can continue to pay premiums until finally they just give up, and their workers are no longer getting insured, and that’s been the trend line.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Or, alternatively, we can figure out, how do we make the cost of care more effective?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And there are ways of doing it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So at Cleveland Clinic, one of the best health care systems in the world, they actually provide great care cheaper than average.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason they do is because they do some smart things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: They — they say, if a patient’s coming in, let’s get all the doctors together at once, do one test instead of having the patient run around with 10 tests.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s make sure that we’re providing preventive care so we’re catching the onset of something like diabetes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let’s — let’s pay providers on the basis of performance as opposed to on the basis of how many procedures they’ve — they’ve engaged in.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Now, so what this board does is basically identifies best practices and says, let’s use the purchasing power of Medicare and Medicaid to help to institutionalize all these good things that we do.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the fact of the matter is that, when Obamacare is fully implemented, we’re going to be in a position to show that costs are going down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And over the last two years, health care premiums have gone up — it’s true — but they’ve gone up slower than any time in the last 50 years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we’re already beginning to see progress.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In the meantime, folks out there with insurance, you’re already getting a rebate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me make one last point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney says, we should replace it, I’m just going to repeal it, but — but we can replace it with something.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But the problem is, he hasn’t described what exactly we’d replace it with, other than saying we’re going to leave it to the states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But the fact of the matter is that some of the prescriptions that he’s offered, like letting you buy insurance across state lines, there’s no indication that that somehow is going to help somebody who’s got a pre-existing condition be able to finally buy insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact, it’s estimated that by repealing Obamacare, you’re looking at 50 million people losing health insurance…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: … at a time when it’s vitally important.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well…

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, actually it’s — it’s — it’s a lengthy description.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But, number one, preexisting conditions are covered under my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Number two, young people are able to stay on their family plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s already offered in the private marketplace.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You don’t have to have the government mandate that for that to occur.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But let’s come back to something the president and I agree on, which is the key task we have in health care is to get the cost down so it’s more affordable for families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then he has as a model for doing that a board of people at the government, an unelected board, appointed board, who are going to decide what kind of treatment you ought to have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In my opinion, the government is not effective in — in bringing down the cost of almost anything.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: As a matter of fact, free people and free enterprises trying to find ways to do things better are able to be more effective in bringing down the cost than the government will ever be.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Your example of the Cleveland Clinic is my case in point, along with several others I could describe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is the private market.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: These are small — these are enterprises competing with each other, learning how to do better and better jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I used to consult to businesses — excuse me, to hospitals and to health care providers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I was astonished at the creativity and innovation that exists in the American people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In order to bring the cost of health care down, we don’t need to have a board of 15 people telling us what kinds of treatments we should have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We instead need to put insurance plans, providers, hospitals, doctors on target such that they have an incentive, as you say, performance pay, for doing an excellent job, for keeping costs down, and that’s happening.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Innermountain Healthcare does it superbly well, Mayo Clinic is doing it superbly well, Cleveland Clinic, others.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the right answer is not to have the federal government take over health care and start mandating to the providers across America, telling a patient and a doctor what kind of treatment they can have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s the wrong way to go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The private market and individual responsibility always work best.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me just point out first of all this board that we’re talking about can’t make decisions about what treatments are given.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s explicitly prohibited in the law.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But let’s go back to what Governor Romney indicated, that under his plan, he would be able to cover people with preexisting conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, actually Governor, that isn’t what your plan does.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What your plan does is to duplicate what’s already the law, which says if you are out of health insurance for three months, then you can end up getting continuous coverage and an insurance company can’t deny you if you’ve — if it’s been under 90 days.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But that’s already the law and that doesn’t help the millions of people out there with preexisting conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: There’s a reason why Governor Romney set up the plan that he did in Massachusetts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It wasn’t a government takeover of health care.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It was the largest expansion of private insurance.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what it does say is that “insurers, you’ve got to take everybody.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” Now, that also means that you’ve got more customers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But when — when Governor Romney says that he’ll replace it with something, but can’t detail how it will be in fact replaced and the reason he set up the system he did in Massachusetts was because there isn’t a better way of dealing with the preexisting conditions problem.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It just reminds me of, you know, he says that he’s going to close deductions and loopholes for his tax plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how it’s going to be paid for, but we don’t know the details.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He says that he’s going to replace Dodd-Frank, Wall Street reform, but we don’t know exactly which ones.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He won’t tell us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: He now says he’s going to replace Obamacare and ensure that all the good things that are in it are going to be in there and you don’t have to worry.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And at some point, I think the American people have to ask themselves, is the reason that Governor Romney is keeping all these plans to replace secret because they’re too good?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Is it — is it because that somehow middle-class families are going to benefit too much from them?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The reason is, is because, when we reform Wall Street, when we tackle the problem of pre-existing conditions, then, you know, these are tough problems and we’ve got to make choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the choices we’ve made have been ones that ultimately are benefiting middle-class families all across the country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: No.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I have to respond to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Which is — which is my experience as a governor is if I come in and — and lay down a piece of legislation and say, “It’s my way or the highway,” I don’t get a lot done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What I do is the same way that Tip O’Neill and Ronald Reagan worked together some years ago.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: When Ronald Reagan ran for office, he laid out the principles that he was going to foster.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said he was going to lower tax rates.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: He said he was going to broaden the base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ve said the same thing, you’re going to simplify the tax code, broaden the base.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Those are my principles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I want to bring down the tax burden on middle-income families.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I’m going to work together with Congress to say, OK, what — what are the various ways we could bring down deductions, for instance?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One way, for instance, would be to have a single number.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Make up a number, $25,000, $50,000.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Anybody can have deductions up to that amount.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And then that number disappears for high-income people.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s one way one could do it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: One could follow Bowles-Simpson as a model and take deduction by deduction and make differences that way.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There are alternatives to accomplish the objective I have, which is to bring down rates, broaden the base, simplify the code, and create incentives for growth.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And with regards to health care, you had remarkable details with regards to my pre-existing condition plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You obviously studied up on — on my plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In fact, I do have a plan that deals with people with pre-existing conditions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That’s part of my health care plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And what we did in Massachusetts is a model for the nation state by state.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I said that at that time.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The federal government taking over health care for the entire nation and whisking aside the 10th Amendment, which gives states the rights for these kinds of things, is not the course for America to have a stronger, more vibrant economy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, I definitely think there are differences.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The first role of the federal government is to keep the American people safe.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s its most basic function.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as commander-in-chief, that is something that I’ve worked on and thought about every single day that I’ve been in the Oval Office.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I also believe that government has the capacity, the federal government has the capacity to help open up opportunity and create ladders of opportunity and to create frameworks where the American people can succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Look, the genius of America is the free enterprise system and freedom and the fact that people can go out there and start a business, work on an idea, make their own decisions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But as Abraham Lincoln understood, there are also some things we do better together.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So, in the middle of the Civil War, Abraham Lincoln said, let’s help to finance the Transcontinental Railroad, let’s start the National Academy of Sciences, let’s start land grant colleges, because we want to give these gateways of opportunity for all Americans, because if all Americans are getting opportunity, we’re all going to be better off.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That doesn’t restrict people’s freedom.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That enhances it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so what I’ve tried to do as president is to apply those same principles.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And when it comes to education what I’ve said is we’ve got to reform schools that are not working.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: We use something called Race to the Top.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Wasn’t a top-down approach, Governor.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: What we’ve said is to states, we’ll give you more money if you initiate reforms.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as a consequence, you had 46 states around the country who have made a real difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But what I’ve also said is let’s hire another 100,000 math and science teachers to make sure we maintain our technological lead and our people are skilled and able to succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And hard-pressed states right now can’t all do that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: In fact we’ve seen layoffs of hundreds of thousands of teachers over the last several years, and Governor Romney doesn’t think we need more teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I do, because I think that that is the kind of investment where the federal government can help.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It can’t do it all, but it can make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And as a consequence we’ll have a better trained workforce and that will create jobs because companies want to locate in places where we’ve got a skilled workforce.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, first, I love great schools.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Massachusetts, our schools are ranked number one of all 50 states.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the key to great schools, great teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So I reject the idea that I don’t believe in great teachers or more teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Every school district, every state should make that decision on their own.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The role of government: Look behind us.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The Constitution and the Declaration of Independence.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The role of government is to promote and protect the principles of those documents.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: First, life and liberty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have a responsibility to protect the lives and liberties of our people, and that means a military second to none.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I do not believe in cutting our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I believe in maintaining the strength of America’s military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Second, in that line that says we are endowed by our creator with our rights, I believe we must maintain our commitment to religious tolerance and freedom in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: That statement also says that we are endowed by our creator with the right to pursue happiness as we choose.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I interpret that as, one, making sure that those people who are less fortunate and can’t care for themselves are cared by — by one another.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re a nation that believes that we’re all children of the same god and we care for those that have difficulties, those that are elderly and have problems and challenges, those that are disabled.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We care for them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And we — we look for discovery and innovation, all these things desired out of the American heart to provide the pursuit of happiness for our citizens.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But we also believe in maintaining for individuals the right to pursue their dreams and not to have the government substitute itself for the rights of free individuals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And what we’re seeing right now is, in my view, a — a trickle-down government approach, which has government thinking it can do a better job than free people pursuing their dreams.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And it’s not working.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the proof of that is 23 million people out of work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The proof of that is 1 out of 6 people in poverty.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The proof of that is we’ve gone from 32 million on food stamps to 47 million on food stamps.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The proof of that is that 50 percent of college graduates this year can’t find work.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We know that the path we’re taking is not working.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s time for a new path.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Well, the primary responsibility for education is — is, of course, at the state and local level.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But the federal government also can play a very important role.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I — and I agree with Secretary Arne Duncan, he’s — some ideas he’s put forward on Race to the Top, not all of them, but some of them I agree with and — and congratulate him for pursuing that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The federal government can get local and — and state schools to do a better job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: My own view, by the way, is I’ve added to that.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I happen to believe, I want the kids that are getting federal dollars from IDEA or Title I — these are disabled kids or — or — or poor kids or — or lower-income kids, rather, I want them to be able to go to the school of their choice.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So all federal funds, instead of going to the — to the state or to the school district, I’d have go, if you will, follow the child and let the parent and the child decide where to send their — their — their student.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, as I’ve indicated, I think that it has a significant role to play.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Through our Race to the Top program, we’ve worked with Republican and Democratic governors to initiate major reforms, and they’re having an impact right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, this is where budgets matter, because budgets reflect choices.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So when Governor Romney indicates that he wants to cut taxes and potentially benefit folks like me and him, and to pay for it we’re having to initiate significant cuts in federal support for education, that makes a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, his — his running mate, Congressman Ryan, put forward a budget that reflects many of the principles that Governor Romney’s talked about.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And it wasn’t very detailed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: This seems to be a trend.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But — but what it did do is to — if you extrapolated how much money we’re talking about, you’d look at cutting the education budget by up to 20 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to community colleges, we are seeing great work done out there all over the country because we have the opportunity to train people for jobs that exist right now.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And one of the things I suspect Governor Romney and I probably agree on is getting businesses to work with community colleges so that they’re setting up their training programs…

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me just finish the point.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The — where they’re partnering so that they’re designing training programs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And people who are going through them know that there’s a job waiting for them if they complete it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That makes a big difference, but that requires some federal support.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Let me just say one final example.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When it comes to making college affordable, whether it’s two-year or four-year, one of the things that I did as president was we were sending $60 billion to banks and lenders as middlemen for the student loan program, even though the loans were guaranteed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So there was no risk for the banks or the lenders, but they were taking billions out of the system.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And we said, “Why not cut out the middleman?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” And as a consequence, what we’ve been able to do is to provide millions more students assistance, lower or keep low interest rates on student loans.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And this is an example of where our priorities make a difference.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Governor Romney, I genuinely believe cares about education, but when he tells a student that, you know, “you should borrow money from your parents to go to college,” you know, that indicates the degree to which, you know, there may not be as much of a focus on the fact that folks like myself, folks like Michelle, kids probably who attend University of Denver, just don’t have that option.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And for us to be able to make sure that they’ve got that opportunity and they can walk through that door, that is vitally important not just to those kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: It’s how we’re going to grow this economy over the long term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President, you’re entitled as the president to your own airplane and to your own house, but not to your own facts.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: All right, I’m not going to cut education funding.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t have any plan to cut education funding and — and grants that go to people going to college.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m planning on to grow.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: So I’m not planning on making changes there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But you make a very good point, which is that the place you put your money just makes a pretty clear indication of where your heart is.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You put $90 billion into — into green jobs.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And I — look, I’m all in favor of green energy.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: $90 billion, that would have — that would have hired 2 million teachers.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: $90 billion.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And these businesses, many of them have gone out of business, I think about half of them, of the ones have been invested in have gone out of business.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: A number of them happened to be owned by people who were contributors to your campaigns.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Look, the right course for America’s government, we were talking about the role of government, is not to become the economic player, picking winners and losers, telling people what kind of health treatment they can receive, taking over the health care system that has existed in this country for a long, long time and has produced the best health records in the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The right answer for government is say, How do we make the private sector become more efficient and more effective?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: How do we get schools to be more competitive?

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Let’s grade them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I propose we grade our schools so parents know which schools are succeeding and failing, so they can take their child to a — to a school that he’s being more successful.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t want to cut our commitment to education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I wanted to make it more effective and efficient.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And by the way, I’ve had that experience.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I don’t just talk about it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve been there.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Massachusetts schools are ranked number one in the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is not because I didn’t have commitment to education.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s because I care about education for all of our kids.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You’ve done a great job.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Jim, I had the great experience — it didn’t seem like it at the time — of being elected in a state where my legislature was 87 percent Democrat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And that meant I figured out from day one I had to get along and I had to work across the aisle to get anything done.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We drove our schools to be number one in the nation.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We cut taxes 19 times.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We — as president, I will sit on day one — actually, the day after I get elected — I’ll sit down with leaders — the Democratic leaders, as well as Republican leaders, and continue — as we did in my state — we met every Monday for a couple hours, talked about the issues and the challenges in the — in the — in our state in that case.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We have to work on a collaborative basis, not because we’re going to compromise our principle, but because there’s common ground.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And the challenges America faces right now — look, the reason I’m in this race is there are people that are really hurting today in this country.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And we face — this deficit could crush the future generations.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What’s happening in the Middle East, there are developments around the world that are of real concern.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And Republicans and Democrats both love America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But we need to have leadership — leadership in Washington that will actually bring people together and get the job done and could not care less if — if it’s a Republican or a Democrat.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ve done it before.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll do it again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, first of all, I think Governor Romney’s going to have a busy first day, because he’s also going to repeal Obamacare, which will not be very popular among Democrats as you’re sitting down with them.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But, look, my philosophy has been, I will take ideas from anybody, Democrat or Republican, as long as they’re advancing the cause of making middle-class families stronger and giving ladders of opportunity to the middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how we cut taxes for middle- class families and small businesses.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how we cut a trillion dollars of spending that wasn’t advancing that cause.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how we signed three trade deals into law that are helping us to double our exports and sell more American products around the world.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how we repealed “don’t ask/don’t tell.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: ” That’s how we ended the war in Iraq, as I promised, and that’s how we’re going to wind down the war in Afghanistan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: That’s how we went after Al Qaida and bin Laden.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: So we’ve — we’ve seen progress even under Republican control of the House of Representatives.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But, ultimately, part of being principled, part of being a leader is, A, being able to describe exactly what it is that you intend to do, not just saying, “I’ll sit down,” but you have to have a plan.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Number two, what’s important is occasionally you’ve got to say no, to — to — to folks both in your own party and in the other party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And, you know, yes, have we had some fights between me and the Republicans when — when they fought back against us reining in the excesses of Wall Street?

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Absolutely, because that was a fight that needed to be had.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: When — when we were fighting about whether or not we were going to make sure that Americans had more security with their health insurance and they said no, yes, that was a fight that we needed to have.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so part of leadership and governing is both saying what it is that you are for, but also being willing to say no to some things.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I’ve got to tell you, Governor Romney, when it comes to his own party during the course of this campaign, has not displayed that willingness to say no to some of the more extreme parts of his party.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: Well, Jim, I want to thank you, and I want to thank Governor Romney, because I think was a terrific debate, and I very much appreciate it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And I want to thank the University of Denver.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, four years ago, we were going through a major crisis.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And yet my faith and confidence in the American future is undiminished.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And the reason is because of its people, because of the woman I met in North Carolina who decided at 55 to go back to school because she wanted to inspire her daughter and now has a job from that new training that she’s gotten; because a company in Minnesota who was willing to give up salaries and perks for their executives to make sure that they didn’t lay off workers during a recession.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: The auto workers that you meet in Toledo or Detroit take such pride in building the best cars in the world, not just because of a paycheck, but because it gives them that sense of pride, that they’re helping to build America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And so the question now is how do we build on those strengths.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And everything that I’ve tried to do, and everything that I’m now proposing for the next four years in terms of improving our education system or developing American energy or making sure that we’re closing loopholes for companies that are shipping jobs overseas and focusing on small businesses and companies that are creating jobs here in the United States, or closing our deficit in a responsible, balanced way that allows us to invest in our future.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: All those things are designed to make sure that the American people, their genius, their grit, their determination, is — is channeled and — and they have an opportunity to succeed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And everybody’s getting a fair shot.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And everybody’s getting a fair share — everybody’s doing a fair share, and everybody’s playing by the same rules.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: You know, four years ago, I said that I’m not a perfect man and I wouldn’t be a perfect president.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: And that’s probably a promise that Governor Romney thinks I’ve kept.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: But I also promised that I’d fight every single day on behalf of the American people, the middle class, and all those who were striving to get into the middle class.

transcript_turns.speaker: Barack Obama
transcript_turns.text: I’ve kept that promise and if you’ll vote for me, then I promise I’ll fight just as hard in a second term.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim, and Mr.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: President.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And thank you for tuning in this evening.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: This is a — this is an important election and I’m concerned about America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’m concerned about the direction America has been taking over the last four years.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I — I know this is bigger than an election about the two of us as individuals.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s bigger than our respective parties.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: It’s an election about the course of America.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: What kind of America do you want to have for yourself and for your children.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And there really are two very different paths that we began speaking about this evening, and over the course of this month we’re going to have two more presidential debates and a vice presidential debate.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’re talk about those two paths.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: But they lead in very different directions.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And it’s not just looking to our words that you have to take in evidence of where they go.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You can look at the record.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: There’s no question in my mind that if the president were to be reelected you’ll continue to see a middle-class squeeze with incomes going down and prices going up.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll get incomes up again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ll see chronic unemployment.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ve had 43 straight months with unemployment above 8 percent.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If I’m president I will create — help create 12 million new jobs in this country with rising incomes.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If the president’s reelected, Obamacare will be fully installed.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: In my view that’s going to mean a whole different way of life for people who counted on the insurance plan they had in the past.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Many will lose it.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’re going to see health premiums go up by some $2,500 per family.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If I’m elected we won’t have Obama.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: We’ll put in place the kind of principles that I put in place in my own state and allow each state to craft their own programs to get people insured and we’ll focus on getting the cost of health care down.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: If the president were to be reelected you’re going to see a $716 billion cut to Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ll have 4 million people who will lose Medicare Advantage.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: You’ll have hospital and providers that’ll no longer accept Medicare patients.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I’ll restore that $716 billion to Medicare.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: And finally, military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The president’s reelected you’ll see dramatic cuts to our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: The secretary of defense has said these would be even devastating.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will not cut our commitment to our military.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: I will keep America strong and get America’s middle class working again.

transcript_turns.speaker: Mitt Romney
transcript_turns.text: Thank you, Jim.
